subject: Bone broth protocol proposed for a person with stage 4 cancer and liver cirrhosis
headline_verdict: NO — no broth, spice or cooking method destroys cancer cells or reverses cirrhosis. Value is supportive nutrition only.

claims.claim: A turmeric/cinnamon broth destroys cancer cells
claims.evidence: Critical analysis of curcumin clinical trials concludes studies failed to convincingly demonstrate significant positive effect in malignant disease; 'use of curcumin in malignant diseases is not justified scientifically' at present.
No mechanism and no evidence. 12-18h IS however correct practice for beef bones on culinary grounds (collagen to gelatin conversion), so the duration was retained.

claims.claim: Eating bone marrow cleanses the liver and reverses cirrhosis
claims.evidence: Marrow is predominantly fat. No cleansing mechanism exists; the liver is not a filter accumulating flushable residue. Marrow does not affect fibrosis. Retains genuine value as a dense calorie source in malnutrition.

Fibrosis regression is well documented, driven by treating the underlying aetiology: alcohol cessation, HBV/HCV antivirals, weight loss in MASLD. Nutrition supports the body while those work; it is not the lever.

claims.claim: Turmeric should be potentiated with black pepper for absorption
claims.evidence: 20mg piperine raises curcumin bioavailability ~20x. This is precisely the pattern implicated in turmeric-associated DILI; DILIN published a ten-case series. Mechanisms: HLA-B*35:01-linked immune-mediated injury, and a dose-dependent antioxidant-to-pro-oxidant flip generating ROS and hepatocyte apoptosis.

claims.claim: Cinnamon is safe for a person with liver disease
claims.evidence: Cassia ~1% coumarin vs Ceylon ~0.004% (~250x). EFSA TDI 0.1 mg/kg bw (~7mg/70kg adult). One tsp cassia = 7-20mg coumarin. Case: 23-year-old hospitalised with hepatitis after 1-2g cinnamon daily for two months.

claims.claim: Protein should be restricted in liver disease
claims.evidence: EASL: stable cirrhosis 1.2-1.5 g/kg IBW/day; sarcopenia 1.5 g/kg. Sarcopenia is a hard prognostic factor. Muscle handles ammonia when the liver cannot, so losing muscle worsens the encephalopathy restriction was meant to prevent.

claims.claim: Bone broth is a good protein source
claims.evidence: Collagen contains zero tryptophan and is incomplete under PDCAAS; also low in methionine and in the BCAAs that matter most in cirrhosis. Rich in glycine/proline/hydroxyproline. Use as a carrier for complete protein, not as the protein.

claims.claim: A salty reduced broth plus Mediterranean salads is appropriate
claims.evidence: Target <2g sodium/day (~90 mEq, ~5.2g salt). Prepared broths are named as high-sodium items to avoid. Mitigation: zero salt in the pot, salt at the bowl. Counter-caution: sodium restriction reduces palatability and can worsen intake; liberalise if malnourished.

claims.claim: Raw shellfish is fine as part of a Mediterranean pattern
claims.evidence: Cirrhosis is the major risk factor for Vibrio vulnificus septicaemia, mortality on the order of 50%. Hard rule: cooked shellfish only.

claims.claim: Bone broth carries a meaningful heavy-metal risk
claims.evidence: Monro et al.: broths contain several times the lead of their source water (chicken bone broth 7.01 ug/L; skin and cartilage 9.5 ug/L). Counterweight: later analysis found Pb/Cd risk minimal at a few ug per serving. Note the same paper undercuts the mineral claims FOR broth (Ca/Mg <5% RDA per serving).

claims.claim: A late-evening snack matters in cirrhosis
claims.evidence: Cirrhotic livers hold little glycogen, so an overnight fast drives catabolism and muscle loss. EASL recommends a late-evening snack; research notes patients often miss it despite its importance. Zero cost, no prescription.
